Since I took the time to type it all out, I decided to go ahead and post here - this is my 'how to life' guide. A number of folks probably won't like it, but it's worked for me so far...so shrug.

Original Question:

What's your life advice to a 19 year old kid trying to do something with his life?

No matter what you end up doing, own it. If your job is literally shoveling shit, do your best and shovel the fuck out of that shit - be the best shit shoveler that has ever shoveled shit in the land! Study shit and shovels in your spare time - master the art and ascend to the role of mentoring others while they shovel shit - all without ever having to sully your hands again.

People who put their all into something (whether they like it or not, because nobody cares if you like it - but it's still your name on the end result) tend to get noticed and move on to better things. Pride - take pride in what you do and your own end result, regardless of what it is - your work is you, yourr business card, your public Facebook profile, it's the thing people will judge you by - change it if you have to, until you find something you can stand, but don't shit on it. If you do, all anyone will see is some shitty kid who has no sense of healthy pride or self-worth. Find something about it you do enjoy, and step up when called to take responsibility for a particular pile of this metaphorical shit - with eyes on you now, make that shit shine!

Own your mistakes and don't blame others (and learn clever, but still honest, wordplay for when it's truly not your fault - nobody likes a full-on tattle tale) - if you're half decent at what you do people will see this as a strength - especially if, later on, you demonstrate that you've learned something from said mistake (don't point it out or rub it in - that's boasting and poorly received). Few people are willing to learn these days - if you are, and especially if you're willing to learn both on your own and from others - humbly and with enthusiasm - you'll be seen as that diamond in the rough, and people will be willing to help polish you.

Now, for the first few years of your adulthood, you'll probably hate your job - don't give in, instead do your best and work your way up and out. Your peers who slacked off and complained/threw others under the bus will still be bitching about your entry-level position when you're their boss (or boss' boss).

15/hr isn't much - ~31,000/year pre-tax. Add in transportation, house/apt, food, bills, fun (for sanity's sake), and other necessities - that doesn't go far, even if you live alone. But - that's a great start for someone who is young. Do well and move up - stagnation is the enemy (and those dollars are worth less and less as time passes) - don't burn yourself out too early though. Don't let yourself become a doormat, but understand that until you stick out as special, well...you're just another disposable cog and there is no sympathy out there for cogs - in fact some psychopaths seek them out just because they're that much easier to abuse.

And, most importantly, learn to read. Not just knowing what sounds the letters make, but understanding what the words mean when arranged in the given order. Too many kids these days can't think. I show them A = B and B = C - when I ask them if A = C, they flail and falter. Read, understand, and at least try to figure something out for yourself (time permitting) before asking - if you share what you learned while researching, and show effort, you'll be rewarded with both the answer to your question and respect for trying. Note that during a fire is not the best time to stop in the stairwell and google what to do if fire - learn to interpret those situations, you don't want to be the one who got in the way and caused more trouble.

Read How to Win Friends & Influence People (don't let the title throw you - and try not to look at it through a sociopath's lens - there are good lessons in there) and don't be a lazy fuck. You don't have to give in to mediocrity, but attaining awesome doesn't come without a fair bit of effort (and patience) on your part - that said (again), if you're getting fucked, get the fuck out and try somewhere else; people are shit and finding the good ones is akin to playing Where's Waldo at a red/white stripey shirt convention.

Some of the above may come easy, some may require a few failures before you get it - that's understandable, not ideal, but still something you can work with. Just make sure you're being honest with yourself when you say but I didn't do aaaaanything wrong, it's everysingleotherfucker ever (that's a difficult one - even if you can't find personal fault, at least keep those thoughts to yourself - a shoddy bridge is still a bridge).

And - that all may not work. Life isn't fair, people are shit, and you're not entitled to anything. Maybe the best you can hope for is to look back and say I am damn proud of everything I did sure beats I fucked everything up, hate myself, have nothing to be proute of/no legacy, and still didn't get ahead, eh?
